winner_in_my_two: DUTY MARKED: LOST — 4th of 9, beaten 2L, at SP 14/1 (banked 15/2 at 08:36Z; DRIFTED 15/2 to 14/1 while the favourite Double Rush came in 9/4 to 6/5F — the board went against the pick all day and the sitting banked before it could see it); each-way 3 places at 1/5: 4th pays nothing, both halves lost; paper level stake −1.00
error: WINNER: Extremely Zain 9/2 (Haggas/Fallon, 3yo colt, 126lb — receiving 4lb from the older horses): my sheet had him SIXTH on the ladder ('rung 7 best, 7th of 9 in the Hungerford G2, made no impression') and passed him on the run; a York COURSE AND DISTANCE winner (the 19-runner handicap off 93, the race's own signpost), 4th in the Ascot International heritage handicap, back to 6f at his winning track after a 7f Group 2 step too far; Double Rush 6/5F 2nd beaten 0.5L (the STORY horse, the market's first, my second danger); Dickensian 40/1 3rd; REGIONAL 4th a further 1L back (14/1); America Queen 100/30 EIGHTH (my named danger, beaten 9L+)
calibration: winner_in_my_two: NO — neither the pick nor the named danger; the second danger (Double Rush, the market's first) was 2nd; the winner was the market's fourth (5/1 morning, 9/2 SP) and the ladder's sixth
column8: ERROR (one sentence): I ranked the best line EVER PLACED (Regional's Minster G2 3rd in May, on an 8yo who was 0-5 this year with four declining lines since — 10th, 9th, 6th — and who the market drifted 15/2 to 14/1 before the off) above the best line ON THE RISE (a 3yo Haggas colt's C&D win here in a 19-runner handicap and a heritage-handicap 4th, the most recent quality form at this exact course and trip), and I wrote the risk down in my own grade ('an 8yo's class against a filly's form') and took it anyway — the class line is a fact but a four-month-old line on a horse whose every line since is worse is a STORY in a class coat, and the market's direction (9th in his order) was the fact I banked without
column9: CALIBRATION: (1) THE FAULT NAMED: 'the highest rung ever' is not 'the best horse today' — the inversion (05 Sep) ranks by best_class_level over the last ten same-code runs and asks nothing about the CURVE of the lines since; today the ladder's #1 was the oldest and coldest horse in the race and the winner was the horse whose lines were rising at this course and distance; the master's own order has 'class is permanent' THIRD, behind 'best horse wins' and 'past winners' — I treated the third as the first. (2) THE DIRECTION, AGAIN: banked 08:36Z at 15/2, SP 14/1; the favourite 9/4 to 6/5; yesterday's Thirsk (Proposal 2/1 out to 4/1, the winner 9/4 in to 5/4) was the same board going the same way — two duties running, the drift named the loser both times. This is the receipt for MONDAY'S CUT (his word 05 Sep: 'we don't really need to do the nap so early?'): the 07:30 read makes the shortlist, the 12:30 board's direction makes the bet. Nothing is carved from this; it is his ruling to give, and the cut is on the plan already. (3) THE DANGER WAS WRONG TOO: America Queen 8th; the market's first (Double Rush) ran 2nd — bot A's record (winner in the market's 1st/2nd in 6 of 9 danger-wins) said name the market's first as the danger; I named the form horse and passed the favourite as 'a handicapper'. (4) THE SIGNPOST I PASSED: Extremely Zain's C&D win at York (won here, this trip, in a 19-runner handicap — the 'ran well here' dot) was on my own sheet and I ranked it seventh on rung alone; the class ladder needs the DIRECTION of the lines beside the rung (the Gower Prince law 3b, 'direction outranks state', already validated) — PROPOSED for his ruling, not carved: on equal or near rungs, the horse whose last three lines are improving beats the horse whose last three are declining, whatever the older peak. (5) RECORD: the duty settles LOST; the engine had no opinion today (the 07:30 run crashed, fixed in #111); the day's yardstick rows still bank from the box's guard and grade tonight — and the shadow ladder's first night will show what key-class did with this race (it would have picked Regional too; the fault is in the KEY, and the shadow is where it gets measured).
